what_it_is.prose: The Astra is India's indigenous beyond-visual-range (BVR) air-to-air missile family, designed by the Research Centre Imarat (RCI) of DRDO in Hyderabad and produced by Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL). The Astra Mk-1, the initial production variant, has a range of approximately 110 km, uses mid-course INS/data-link guidance with terminal active radar homing, and carries a high-explosive fragmentation warhead. It is operational with the Indian Air Force on the Su-30MKI and has been integrated on the Tejas Mk-1/1A. The Astra Mk-2 is in advanced development with an extended range of approximately 160 km, featuring a dual-pulse rocket motor for improved kinematics. The Astra Mk-3 (also referred to as SFDR — Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet) is under development and aims to provide beyond-BVR range (potentially 300+ km) using ramjet propulsion. The Astra family represents a significant step in India's quest for air-to-air missile self-reliance, reducing dependence on Russian (R-77) and Israeli (Derby, Python-5) BVR missiles.

faq.question: What is the range of the Astra missile?
faq.answer: The Astra Mk-1 has a range of approximately 110 km (beyond visual range). The Astra Mk-2, in advanced development, aims for approximately 160 km with a dual-pulse rocket motor. The Astra Mk-3 / SFDR is under development and aims for 300+ km using ramjet propulsion.

faq.question: Which aircraft can carry the Astra?
faq.answer: The Astra Mk-1 is currently integrated on the Su-30MKI and Tejas Mk-1/1A. Future integration is planned for the Tejas Mk-2, AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft), and any future MRFA winner. The missile can be carried on standard NATO/station-compatible hardpoints.

faq.question: How does Astra compare to the R-77 and Derby missiles?
faq.answer: The Astra Mk-1 (~110 km) has comparable range to the Russian R-77 (~80-100 km) and exceeds the Israeli Derby (~50 km). The Astra uses an indigenous active radar seeker and mid-course data-link, making it a viable replacement for imported BVR missiles on Indian fighter aircraft. The Mk-2 variant (~160 km) will exceed the range of both the R-77 and Derby.
